jamie (Product): Quick drop — draft PRD for field-level output contracts + tool/function interop. Need a quick take on acceptance criteria, launch must-haves, and priority tradeoffs. Draft link: https://internal.redwood/prd/field-output-contracts 
anya (Eng): Skimmed — big risk is per-field KV cache + schema version skew. Suggest adding a 'Contract-Version' header in responses and SDKs that can opt into strict validation.
rob (ML Spec): Agreed. Also call out numeric normalization rules. Edge case: model returns 'N/A' for an integer field — decide canonical handling (coerce / error / map-to-null).
liz (Design): UX question: how do we surface soft vs hard validation to devs? Propose a per-field "validationSeverity" with levels: warn, block. UI should surface examples and a migration guide.
maya (CS): We've had 2 customers ask for warning-first then opt-in to block. Migration docs and sample prompts are required. +1 to per-field severity.
ty (QA): QA checklist notes: fuzz with mixed types, missing fields, extra fields, nullables, nested arrays. Automate a regression harness that runs against model variants.
steve (API): API changes to propose: add response header X-Output-Contract-Version and a query param ?validate=(strict|lenient|off). Keep default backward compatible.
anya (Eng): Implementation note: fallback policy should prefer a structured fallback — if strict schema fails, attempt to parse into a fallback 'tool_call' envelope with raw args string, then emit telemetry and optionally surface as warning.
rob (ML Spec): Sample contract snippet for clarity:
```json
{"fields": [{"name":"price","type":"number","nullable":false,"validationSeverity":"block"},{"name":"notes","type":"string","nullable":true,"validationSeverity":"warn"}],"version":"2024-06-01"}
```
jamie (Product): Draft acceptance criteria: 1) SDK returns parsed object for non-blocking fields and surfaces per-field warnings; 2) For block-level failures, SDK surfaces a structured validation error (HTTP 400 in hosted API) and emits telemetry with contract id + failure code; 3) Streaming support: partial field delivery allowed, but final validation enforced when stream completes; 4) Rollout: canary 10% + opt-in customers, migration doc and 3 beta customers.
maya (CS): Add to acceptance: signed customer beta agreements from at least 3 customers representing enterprise/regulatory use.
ty (QA): Add tests for race between KV cache and schema updates; streaming edge where field completes mid-stream; fuzzing with long strings and deeply nested arrays.
liz (Design): For streaming UIs we should show parsing progress and flag fields with warnings in-line so devs can triage quickly.
anya (Eng): Timeline check: MVP in one sprint if we cut scope to core validation, header, SDK flag, and basic telemetry. Full rollout (migration tooling, console UI) in next sprint.
jamie (Product): Prioritization outline: must-haves = block/warn semantics, telemetry, SDK opt-in flag; should-haves = console display + migration helper; nice-to-haves = auto-migration tool and per-customer override UI. Customer asks mapped: enterprise = block by default; startups = warn-first.
steve (API): I'll draft the API RFC/PR tomorrow. @infra-bot can you create an RFC thread and allocate tracking?
infra-bot: RFC created: https://internal.redwood/rfcs/482 — please add :thumbsup: and comment threads.
rob (ML Spec): Edge cases to enumerate in RFC: 1) nested arrays with mixed element types 2) ambiguous numeric strings ("1,234" vs "1234") 3) model returns function/tool call but function schema missing 4) circular references or self-referential outputs 5) combining streaming partials with validation rules.
jamie (Product): Thanks — please leave comments on the RFC by EOD Friday. If no major blockers, target canary start 2024-06-20 (customer opt-in).
steve (API): tagging the API PR with the contract draft and a changelog entry for backward compat.
anya (Eng): small implementation detail: add migration header X-Contract-Deprecated-Fields listing removed/renamed fields to help SDKs surface warnings during canary.
maya (CS): I'll reach out to the 3 beta customers this afternoon to confirm interest.
ty (QA): I'll start drafting the regression harness and post a test plan in the RFC thread.
jamie (Product): Great — rough owners assigned: API = steve, SDK + runtime validation = anya, ML edge rules = rob, QA harness = ty, console UX = liz, customer onboarding = maya. Back to the doc folks — comments by EOD Fri. Thanks all :rocket:
